accuracy.evidence: Checked against the English National Curriculum (2014) Year 2 statutory requirement 'apostrophes to mark singular possession in nouns [for example, the girl's name]' and its Year 4 placement of plural possession (the girls' names), Common Core L.2.2c ('use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives'), and the Oxford and Cambridge style rules that a singular noun ending in s still normally takes 's (the bus's, James's) with James' as an accepted variant. Every lab item uses a single owner, so no plural-possession rule is taught wrongly.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS1 errors: apostrophe in a plain plural (greengrocer's apostrophe: the 'Three cats' prediction, two apple's in Fix it, plural tag, m6), mark after the s for one owner (dogs' button in Add the apostrophe with 'The mark after the s means more than one dog', after tag, m4), leaving it out (The dogs bone, none tag), splitting the name (d'ogs), and reversing owner and thing (Mia's cat prediction, hat's Ben tile, order tag, m1, m3).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagposs is built on the mark itself: the owner word is laid out as letter tiles with a gap before every letter, the apostrophe tile must be dropped into the gap between the owner and the s, and the letters slide apart to let it in. Other steps read 's to route a thing to its owner and squash a 'belongs to' phrase into two tiles. Shingle similarity is 9% with flag_sorry.js, 5% with flag_nph.js and under 4% with every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the position by trying gaps: dropping after the s or inside the name bounces with a reason, and only owner-then-'-then-s lights the 'belongs to' arrow from the dog picture to the bone picture. Sorting shows that most words ending in s have no apostrophe; Whose is it? makes the child read 's to find the owner; Say it short shows 's replaces 'that belongs to'. The done text then names the rule.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options that the next task disproves: 'Yes: cat's' for three cats (the sort bins then reject cat's as a plural), and 'The cat owns Mia' for Mia's cat (dragging the cat to Mia is the only move that lands). A.reveal quotes the child's own guess in the done line.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; why() gives a specific correction for each slip: after ('The mark goes right after the owner, before the s. After the s means many owners'), plural ('More than one is just s'), order ('The word with 's is the owner. It comes first'), none ('Without 's we cannot tell it belongs'). Every wrong move inside the lab also names its slip, for example 'Leo's book: look for the word with 's'.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK 0.7 against the family kid target of 5.0, in short concrete sentences ('The dog has a bone. The bone belongs to the dog.'). Adult text measures FK 7.6 against 10.0 and uses precise terms: possessive apostrophe, singular noun, plural possession, possessive its, contraction, greengrocer's apostrophe, with the Year 2 and Grade 2 standard references.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; the explanation's largest 6-word-shingle overlap with any other lesson is 0.2%. Kid paragraphs cover the owner rule, where the mark goes, plural versus belongs, and finding the owner; adult paragraphs give the curriculum placement, the one-owner rule including nouns ending in s, four named mistakes plus the its caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for every step: letter tiles d-o-g-s with visible gaps fit the width with the thing word beside them; the drag apostrophe tile is 56 by 64 px; owner cards show a girl, a cat and a boy picture with names; the four word tiles in Say it short fit one row; young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall and wrap without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme and there were no console errors. Every drag has a button twin (each apostrophe position, each bin, each owner, each word in Fix it plus No mistake, each word tile), and the canvas aria-label is updated with every message.

sources: DfE (2013) English programmes of study: key stages 1 and 2, Year 2 and Year 4 spelling, vocabulary, grammar and punctuation (English Appendix 2)
Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Language L.2.2c
